result.summary:
Independently re-ran MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test on feature/WF02-REQ034-20260817 (commit 05c8488) myself, not sourced from TEST-RUNNER's report. Real output: 'Running ExUnit with seed: 920985, max_cases: 16' ... 'Finished in 27.6 seconds (1.6s async, 25.9s sync)' / '4 properties, 598 tests, 0 failures', shell exit code 0. This matches TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report (test/reports/report-2026-08-17-WF02-REQ034-20260817.yaml) line-for-line ('4 properties, 598 tests, 0 failures') -- consistent, but confirmed by my own independent run, not copied from it. Also ran the REQ-034 test file in isolation as a second check: 'mix test test/letflow/definitions/export_import_test.exs' -> 'Finished in 1.5 seconds (0.00s async, 1.5s sync)' / '5 tests, 0 failures'.

AC-by-AC re-check against actual shipped lib/letflow/definitions/export_import.ex and test/letflow/definitions/export_import_test.exs (not against any agent's summary):

AC1 ("export/1 on an existing definition produces a document whose graph field round-trips byte-for-byte comparable back through import/1's graph field") -- export/2 (export_import.ex:87-100) copies definition.graph verbatim into ExportDocument.graph with no transformation; import/3 (line 120-136) passes document.graph verbatim into create/2's attrs.graph with no transformation. Test 'export/2 + import/3 (AC1)' (export_import_test.exs:204-231) builds a graph with nested extra metadata, asserts document.graph == graph after export, imported.graph == graph after import, AND re-reads the row from Postgres directly (reread!/2) to prove fidelity survives the jsonb encode/decode round trip, not just the in-memory struct chain. Satisfied.

AC2 ("import/1 always assigns a new id distinct from the source document's id field, even when the source id happens to already exist as a definition in the target tenant") -- import/3 never includes document.id in the attrs map passed to Definitions.create/2 (lines 123-129 build attrs with no :id key), so the id is always create/2's autogenerated primary key. Test suite covers both the basic case (export_import_test.exs:240-253, refute imported.id == document.id) and the explicit collision case (255-295: pre-inserts a row in the target tenant under document.id via insert_row_with_id!/4, then asserts the imported row still gets a distinct fresh id AND the pre-existing collision row is left untouched with its original name/version -- proves no overwrite, no merge). Satisfied.

AC3 ("import/1 on a document with a graph that fails REQ-028's validateGraph() is rejected the same way REQ-030's create/1 rejects an invalid graph directly -- no bypass path") -- import/3 performs zero independent structural/attribute validation of its own (moduledoc INV-EI-2, confirmed by reading: the function body is only the schema-version case statement, then a direct pass-through to Definitions.create/2, no intermediate check). Test (export_import_test.exs:305-346) builds a graph_missing_end_node() document, calls both ExportImport.import/3 and a direct Definitions.create/2 with attrs mirroring import/3's own construction, asserts both return the identical {:error, {:graph_validation_failed, violations}} tuple (import_violations == direct_violations, import_result == direct_result), and confirms zero rows written. Satisfied.

AC4 ("import/1 on a document whose bpm_export_schema_version is not 'bpm/definition/v1' is rejected with a distinct unknown-schema-version error") -- import/3's case statement (lines 121-135) checks document.bpm_export_schema_version against @export_schema_version ("bpm/definition/v1") first, before any tenant/database work; a mismatch returns {:error, {:unknown_schema_version, actual}} and never reaches create/2. Test (export_import_test.exs:355-383) uses an otherwise-fully-valid document with bpm_export_schema_version "bpm/definition/v0", asserts the exact {:error, {:unknown_schema_version, "bpm/definition/v0"}} tuple, explicitly refutes it matches the {:error, {:graph_validation_failed, _}} shape (proving the schema gate runs first, not a coincidental validation failure), and confirms zero rows written. Satisfied.

All 4 acceptance criteria confirmed against actual shipped code and tests, independently, not against any prior agent's self-report.

Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-034 status is 'in_progress' (docs/requirements.yaml:1559) -- accurate, has NOT drifted to done prematurely. docs/status/requirement_status.yaml has exactly one event for REQ-034, a 'started' event at 2026-08-17T20:30:32Z (line 3302-3312) -- no 'done' event present yet. Both files currently and correctly reflect 'in progress, not yet done'; neither has drifted ahead of what's actually shipped. Per this handoff's scope, I am NOT flipping either file to done -- that is DOC-UPDATER's job at Step 6.

Incidental: ISS-0036 (filed at WF02-REQ034-20260817's Step 3, github.com/tvolodi/letflow/issues/113) is a pre-existing MINOR warning in an unrelated file (promotion_review_migration_test.exs, an unused default arg) -- confirmed non-blocking, does not affect REQ-034's own test file or code, and was already correctly filed rather than silently fixed in-scope.
